answer: A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The delta multiplier is published, charged in summit, and terrace lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 7 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 2224 identities would post 2530 proofs and burn roughly 70 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
